summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 70.1 of CipherBox (rotation read-plane durability and deep crash-resume soundness) via the GSD workflow: research, plan, verify, and then wave-based parallel execution with git worktrees across 13 plans covering the TS engine, Rust engine twin, and desktop FUSE live-wiring.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans across 7 waves were implemented and merged with green unit/integration gates (sdk-core 363, sdk 362, cargo cipherbox-sdk 146, cargo cipherbox-fuse 106, depth-3 e2e 6/6); two genuine product bugs were found and fixed (dirty-frontier decrypt-before-check ordering in both engines, and desktop refresh_sent_shares never being wired). The final human-gated D-16 desktop-e2e CI acceptance run failed on macOS/Linux at Step 8 setup, and while investigating, a debugger found a second unfixed race (three JsonSidecarFloorStore instances sharing one file with independent locks and a shared tmp path) that a fixer subagent was actively repairing when the session ended.

repo: GSD decision-coverage parser only accepts three D-NN bullet forms (`- **D-NN:**`, `- **D-NN — title**`, `- **D-NN: Title.**`); a bullet like `- **D-NN (title).**` (period before closing `**`) fails to parse and silently zeroes out coverage for ALL decisions in the file, not just the malformed one.
gsd_run loop render-hooks plan:pre --raw emits invalid JSON (literal newlines in fragments) — must read the hooks file directly instead of parsing --raw output.

state.planned-phase and roadmap annotate tools can silently no-op (return updated:[] or updated:false) if STATE.md/ROADMAP.md don't match their expected anchor format — always verify with git diff/status after running them, don't trust the echoed success message.
gsd commit helper can report commit_failed due to slow lint-staged hooks (esp. on large files like ROADMAP.md) while the commit actually lands — always verify via git log, never blind-retry.
Rust rotation engine (crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs) is a structural twin of the TS engine (packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/engine.ts); bugs and fixes in one very likely apply to the other.

crates/fuse write_ops gate logic (grant_scope.rs, delete.rs, rename.rs) determines shared-scope-exit rotation; a same-folder rename never rotates (parent==newparent check), and CipherBox delete is a soft-delete/move-to-bin, which is why deletes under a covering grant DO trigger rotation.

packages/sdk's IndexedDB rotation floor logic (rotation-high-water.ts) is CI-vitest-tested, but historically browser-only migration logic (foldLegacyStoresIntoCombined) lived untested in apps/web (which is web-e2e-gated, not run by CI's Test job) — now hoisted into packages/sdk with fake-indexeddb.

crates/sdk's WriteQueue journal scanner (queue.rs load_all_for_vault/gc_failed_entries) scans every *.json in cb-journal/ and warns 'missing field id' on the co-located rotation-high-water.json floor sidecar — benign since GC only deletes parsed Failed entries by id and .bin orphans, never unparsed .json, but noisy since Phase 69.

CipherBoxFS (crates/fuse/src/fs.rs) held three independently-constructed JsonSidecarFloorStore instances all pointing at the same rotation-high-water.json but each with its own Arc<Mutex>, and write_map_atomic_blocking always used the same deterministic .tmp path — concurrent writers race and the loser's rename() hits ENOENT, causing scope-exit rotation to fail closed.

Desktop mount (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs) never called CipherBoxFS::refresh_sent_shares, so sent_shares cache stayed non-authoritative and D-15a's fail-closed gate caused EIO on every real-mount delete/rename regardless of private/shared.
macOS and Linux desktop-e2e run run-all.sh; Windows runs a separate run-all.ps1 — a new test step added to one script does not automatically run on the other platform.

cargo fmt run unscoped (workspace-wide, e.g. `cargo fmt --all`) strands out-of-scope formatting drift in unrelated files across a worktree; must scope with `-p <package>` to avoid dirtying files outside the plan's declared scope.

code.finding: verify_subtree_clean was non-recursive and treated a missing root record as 'clean' (empty frontier indistinguishable from converged); fixed by widening DirtyFrontierEntry and adding a recursive collect_dirty_frontier helper that returns VerifySubtreeOutcome{is_dirty, frontier}.

collectDirtyFrontier (via resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope ~line 664) unconditionally AEAD-decrypted a child's sealed ref before checking childPub.generation > childRef.generation; for a genuinely dirty edge whose parent also rotated in the same walk, decryption with the current key always throws before the dirtiness check runs — an ordering bug masked by unit-test mocks that made unsealChildReadKey unconditionally succeed.

JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() constructs a fresh Arc<Mutex<()>> per instance; three separate instances (generation_store, seq_store, rotation_checkpoint_store) in CipherBoxFS all target the same rotation-high-water.json file without a shared lock.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally returned Err unconditionally (fail-closed stub) because the only impl RotationDeps in the workspace was the test FakeDeps; live-wired in plan 09 via a new FuseRotationDeps adapter (crates/fuse/src/write_ops/rotation_deps.rs).

workflow: When dispatching multiple worktree-isolated subagents, fire them in separate sequential tool-call messages rather than one parallel batch — simultaneous `git worktree add` calls race on .git/config.lock.

Run a single canary plan through the full worktree→commit→SUMMARY→merge cycle before fanning out a large parallel wave, to validate the harness mechanics early — but communicate this intent to the user upfront so it isn't mistaken for under-parallelizing.

After merging a wave that changed a package's source, rebuild that package's dist before running a consuming package's test suite in the same checkout — stale dist causes false-positive cross-plan test failures that look like real regressions.
When a subagent returns a debug/diagnosis verdict, independently re-verify commits and rerun the relevant test gate yourself rather than trusting the subagent's self-report at face value.

Avoid editing the shared main checkout while a subagent (e.g. a debugger or fixer) is actively building/running against it — queue read-only or isolated-file edits until it returns to avoid corrupting its in-flight build.
Capture newly discovered but out-of-scope follow-up work as explicit GSD todo files immediately, rather than only mentioning them in chat, so they aren't lost when context is compacted.

friction: Decision-coverage gate blocking failure required tracing through the parser source to find a subtle bullet-format mismatch (period vs colon before closing **) affecting pre-existing D-09/D-10 bullets, not the newly added ones.
state.planned-phase tool silently no-op'd (returned updated:[]) requiring manual STATE.md edits.
roadmap annotate tool also returned updated:false as a silent no-op.
render-hooks --raw produced invalid JSON requiring a workaround (reading the file directly).

Wave 1 merge blocked on worktree_dirty from plan 03's unscoped cargo fmt leaving ~13 unrelated files reformatted-but-uncommitted, requiring manual verification it was formatting-only before discarding.
Cross-package dist staleness caused a false-positive 3-test failure after Wave 3 merge (sdk vitest ran against a stale pre-Wave-2 sdk-core dist).

sdk-e2e test harness has no dotenv loader in vitest config, so .env must be sourced manually into the shell before running vitest, else it silently falls back to a default test-login secret producing an opaque 401 instead of a clear config error.

Rust-analyzer showed a stale/false-positive compile error (AncestorChain type mismatch in a nonexistent macros.rs) after plan 11 merged, requiring cross-checking with the authoritative cargo compiler to rule it out.

Debugger subagent misreported its working branch name in its final summary (said feat/phase-70.1-... but was actually on feat/rotation-...soundne with a clean tree), forcing a verification step to rule out an accidental branch switch.

Desktop-e2e CI run failed on macOS/Linux at the newly-authored Step 8 setup (secret.txt never propagated within 90s/18-attempt poll budget) — could not be reproduced locally on a warm machine (~40-47s wall clock for the publish chain), suggesting the poll budget is simply too tight for CI runner speed.

AskUserQuestion was effectively bypassed twice by the user routing follow-up questions directly to the still-running plan-13 subagent instead of answering the orchestrator's structured question, requiring the orchestrator to synthesize answers arriving via task-notifications rather than direct user replies.
open_items: JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer race (three independently-locked instances sharing one file/tmp path) — fixer subagent was actively implementing a per-path shared lock + concurrency test when the session ended; not yet verified or committed.

Journal-warning fix (skip rotation-high-water* filenames in WriteQueue's *.json scan loops) — root-caused and tracked as a task, deferred until after the concurrent fixer finishes to avoid corrupting its build.
shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts poll budget widened 18→40 attempts + timing logging locally but not yet committed or verified against a re-run of CI.
Windows Step 8 (run-all.ps1) added and committed but never actually exercised in a passing CI run yet.
D-16 desktop-e2e real-mount acceptance is still failing (macOS/Linux Step 8) and not yet signed off — phase cannot fully close until this passes.
Secondary unconfirmed anomaly from debugger's local repro: grant-root IPNS sequence bumped by +2 instead of +1 in one run, possibly a symptom of the same floor-store race, not yet root-caused.
WinFsp D-15d gate-ordering parity gap tracked as todo (2026-07-08-winfsp-d15d-gate-ordering-parity.md) — Windows write_ops.rs still has the old ordering, can't be verified on macOS.

Desktop ROT-04 grant re-mint no-op tracked as todo (2026-07-08-desktop-query-grants-rooted-at-remint-noop.md) — desktop query_grants_rooted_at/update_grant/delete_grant are no-ops, so scope-exit rotation currently de-authorizes ALL recipients rather than selectively re-minting for still-authorized ones.
Cosmetic heading inconsistency in Plan 01 ('this phase produces (master index)' vs 'this plan produces') flagged by plan-checker as non-blocking, never cleaned up.
